translationRepairs: In the second year of Chengsheng (552), for repeated battle honors he was raised to marquis, his fief brought to five hundred households in all.
In the second year of Chengsheng (553), for repeated battle honors he was raised to marquis, his fief brought to five hundred households in all.
承聖二年 is Chengsheng year 2. Chengsheng began in AD 552, so year 2 is AD 553; the parenthetical 552 is wrong.
After Sihui was suppressed, in the second year of Shaotai (555) he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, stern-prestige general, and left defender of the heir.
After Sihui was suppressed, in the second year of Shaotai (556) he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, stern-prestige general, and left defender of the heir.
紹泰二年 is Shaotai year 2. Shaotai year 1 is AD 555, so year 2 is AD 556; the parenthetical 555 is wrong.
In the fifth year of Tiancheng (564), Emperor Wen again decreed: "Han worthies were painted in the palace; Wei champions were named in the ancestral shrine—so merit lives on and ages do not forget.
In the fifth year of Tianjia (564), Emperor Wen again decreed: "Han worthies were painted in the palace; Wei champions were named in the ancestral shrine—so merit lives on and ages do not forget.
天嘉五年 uses 嘉, the Chen reign Tianjia; Tiancheng misreads the era name. The replacement restores Tianjia while keeping the correct AD 564.

In the fifth year of Tiancheng, Emperor Wen again issued an edict saying: "Han dynasty meritorious ministers had their forms painted in the palace halls; Wei dynasty fierce generals had their names joined to the ancestral temple—thus merit endures and generations do not forget.

In the fifth year of Tianjia, Emperor Wen again issued an edict saying: "Han dynasty meritorious ministers had their forms painted in the palace halls; Wei dynasty fierce generals had their names joined to the ancestral temple—thus merit endures and generations do not forget.
Same unit: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng. The literal replacement matches the Chinese reign name.
Cheng Lingxi, styled Xuantidi, was a native of Haining in Xin'an.
Cheng Lingxi, styled Xuandi, was a native of Haining in Xin'an.
字玄滌 is a two-character courtesy name Xuandi (玄+滌); Xuantidi invents a third syllable absent from the Chinese.
Cheng Lingxi, styled Xuantidi, was a native of Haining in Xin'an.
Cheng Lingxi, styled Xuandi, was a native of Haining in Xin'an.
Same unit: 玄滌 is Xuandi. The literal replacement removes the invented syllable.
In the fourth year of Tiancheng (563) Zhou Di raided Linchuan again. Lingxi was made commander and, marching from Poyang by a separate route, drove Di back into the hills.
In the fourth year of Tianjia (563) Zhou Di raided Linchuan again. Lingxi was made commander and, marching from Poyang by a separate route, drove Di back into the hills.
天嘉四年 is Tianjia year 4; Tiancheng misreads 嘉. Tianjia restores the correct reign name.

In the fourth year of Tiancheng, Zhou Di again raided Linchuan heavily; Lingxi was made commander-in-chief; from a separate route through Poyang he struck Di, and Di again fled into the mountain valleys.

In the fourth year of Tianjia, Zhou Di again raided Linchuan heavily; Lingxi was made commander-in-chief; from a separate route through Poyang he struck Di, and Di again fled into the mountain valleys.
Same unit: 天嘉 is Tianjia, not Tiancheng. The literal replacement matches the Chinese reign name.
He was posthumously made pacifying-west general and grand master with the golden seal and purple cord, with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
He was posthumously made garrisoning-west general and opener of an office equal to the three dukes, with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
贈鎮西將軍、開府儀同三司 names Garrisoning-West General and opener of an office equal to the three dukes; pacifying-west and golden-seal-and-purple-cord are different titles (安西 / 金紫光祿大夫).
He was posthumously made Pacifying West General and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord; posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
He was posthumously made Garrisoning-West General and Opener of an Office Equal to the Three Dukes; posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
Same unit: 鎮西將軍 and 開府儀同三司 are mistranslated in the literal line; the replacement restores both titles.
In the second year of Tiancheng (561) he was made steadfast-resolution general and administrator of Xin'an, and marched east with Hou Andu against Liu Yi.
In the second year of Tianjia (561) he was made steadfast-resolution general and administrator of Xin'an, and marched east with Hou Andu against Liu Yi.
